summary.headline: Executor is scaffolding a spec-driven orchestration subsystem but has not yet wired it into the app.

findings.title: Executor added SpecManager module plus 455 lines of orchestration types but no integration points

evidence.detail: New 311-line class managing .nexus/specs/<id>/ layout (request.md, spec.vN.md/json, feedback, approval, meta)
Only self-references inside SpecManager.ts — not imported by index.ts, ws/handlers.ts, or any other module yet

findings.impact: The subsystem is currently dead code. If the executor moves on before wiring SpecManager into the server, these types and the class will drift out of sync with the rest of the codebase.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Watch for follow-up edits that register SpecManager in index.ts and handle the new OrchestrationClientEvent/OrchestrationServerEvent message types in ws/handlers.ts.

findings.title: New WebSocket orchestration events are declared in types.ts on both sides but neither side handles them

evidence.detail: OrchestrationClientEvent (spec.generate/revise/approve/cancel/list, plan.*, observer.*) and OrchestrationServerEvent added at lines 526–559
Only appearances are the type declarations themselves — no emit sites, no ws handler case arms

findings.impact: Clients sending any spec.* / plan.* / observer.* event will get no response; the declared protocol cannot be exercised end-to-end.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Check subsequent turns for ws/handlers.ts changes that add case arms for these event types.

findings.title: SpecManager constructor creates .nexus/specs/ but the directory is not yet present on disk

evidence.detail: Constructor calls fs.mkdirSync(this.specsDir, { recursive: true }) on instantiation
Returned: No such file or directory

findings.impact: Confirms SpecManager has never been instantiated in this workspace — consistent with F-001's 'not yet wired' observation.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Once SpecManager is instantiated by the server bootstrap, .nexus/specs/ should appear; ensure it is added to .gitignore alongside .nexus/agents.yaml and .nexus/history/.

findings.title: agents.yaml lists three Claude Code panes as running/idle but the recorded PIDs are the parent shells, not Claude CLIs

evidence.detail: pane-82 (观察者) pid=2323922 status=running, pane-83 (执行者) pid=2324100 status=running, pane-84 (审查者) pid=2324252 status=idle
All three PIDs resolve to /usr/bin/zsh processes (the shell wrapper), not claude CLIs

findings.impact: This is the documented 'shell套壳启动' pattern (CLAUDE.md decision 1), so it is expected — but it means PID-based liveness checks cannot distinguish 'agent running' from 'agent exited, shell alive'. Worth flagging because the previous observation log (2026-04-05) treated analogous stale PIDs as a bug.
findings.suggested_follow_up: Clarify in runtime-state docs that pid is the shell pid; liveness of the agent itself requires a separate signal (statusline heartbeat or output idle time).

findings.title: All three active panes share the same workdir with isolation=shared and the worktree has uncommitted changes

evidence.detail: All three panes (观察者/执行者/审查者) declared isolation: shared
M packages/server/src/types.ts, M packages/web/src/types.ts, ?? packages/server/src/spec/ — uncommitted work from the executor is visible to all panes

findings.impact: With the executor mid-edit on types.ts and a new spec/ directory, any write by the reviewer or observer into the same files would conflict. Current roles suggest this is intentional (reviewer needs to see the executor's changes), but the hot files are not claimed in any mechanism visible here.
findings.suggested_follow_up: If the newly-declared FileClaim / TaskStatusEntry types get wired up, verify that the executor's in-flight edits register claims on types.ts and spec/.
